entry: New: a Copy result button in the Civilization Summary copies a one-line result (eras completed, furthest era, seasons, peak population and sustainability) to share. Earned achievements now have a Share button, and a Credits link sits at the bottom of the page (in the Help menu on Desktop).

New: a setting, on by default, pauses the season clock while this browser tab is hidden and puts your speed back, with a short note, when you return. Turn it off in Settings if you want the clock to keep running in a background tab.

New: name your settlement (Founder's Log window, with era-flavoured suggestions) and see the name on the founding plaque, the Summary, the archive and the shareable card. Export your run as CSV or JSON from the Civilization Summary. Compare any two archived settlements side by side. Par badges for reaching the Relay Age quickly (seasons and time). Achievements are now a row of monuments, one picture per era. A Screensaver mode shows only the slowly turning 3D city (Scene menu, or press S), and you can remap the keyboard shortcuts in Settings.

City Views now shows a small sparkline next to every stat (the last 20 seasons) and a change arrow, and hovering or focusing a stat such as Food, People or the Score opens a little waterfall of the top three things that moved it last season. The Civilization Summary has a new Post-mortem report: what went well, what went wrong, the root cause of the biggest livability drop and three decisions to look at again, written from your stats and Council Minutes.

Desktop layout (first version): on a wide window with a mouse you can choose "Switch to Desktop layout" on the opening screen. It fills the whole window instead of a narrow column. The settlement scene is the whole game: chips along its top show people, food, materials, tools, knowledge and sustainability, and each opens a dropdown with what it will do next season (for example "+1 person per season", or food gathered, eaten and spoiled). Buildings in the scene are the controls for assigning workers, building and research. A few icons (Achievements, City Views, Settings) and a Menu (also Escape) hold everything else, and the log, scenario picker, Look back and Community open as windows over the scene. New log entries pop up briefly, there is a Fullscreen button and a hotkey bar, and the tutorial is rewritten for this layout. Your saves are shared with the Classic layout, which is unchanged and one click away ("Classic layout" in the Menu).

Found a New Settlement: a confirm-gated button files your current settlement in the archive and starts a fresh one, reopening the scenario picker, Hard Mode and consulting cases (also on each archive entry in the Civilization Summary). The new settlement inherits one small founder's legacy from the settlement you just filed: a single named gift, like Seed Stock or Recorded Lessons, chosen by the furthest era it reached, delivered once with your first season. And once you have reached the Space Age in any settlement, a fourth opening unlocks: the Refuge Start, a larger, older group on worn land with too few roofs.

Light mode polish: the theme switch now lives in Settings (the floating Light/Dark pill is gone from this game), the 3D sky and lighting brighten in light mode and re-light the moment you flip the theme, and every panel (readouts, research and consulting-mode text, meters, the Hamlet chips and Town panel, the City Views dashboard, civic map, flow diagram and trajectory chart) now meets text contrast in light mode. Dark mode is unchanged.

Eighth era added: the Relay Age, after the Space Age. The settlement becomes a region: Relay Stations link it to outlying holdings (surface outposts, orbital platforms, first footholds off-world) and Wayfinders haul banked surplus out along the links. A supplied holding opens up new sustainable land; an unsupplied one shrinks that gain and costs equity by the gap between how well the core and the holdings live. New research tiers 15-16, a Relay Age scene, Hamlet station, info-panel sources and two achievements (R2-K26).

New collapsible "In the real world" note for each of the eight eras: a real example behind that era's mechanics (Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük, Uruk, the guilds of Florence, London's Great Stink, Curitiba, the International Space Station, NASA's Commercial Resupply Services), each with a linked source and the date it was read. It changes no game number (W2).

New optional Hamlet view (desktop only, off by default): switch it on and the controls move into the scene itself. Click a building to build more of it or put a worker on it, use the small buttons under each building to take workers off or buy another, and click the Town Centre for research, civic challenges and the next era. Every building is also reachable and usable from the keyboard, and it falls back to a flat map if the 3D view is off (U2).
Seasons now pass on their own. Pause, 1x, 2x and 4x speed controls replace the Advance Season button, and every settlement starts paused (U1).
New Council Minutes panel: a dated ledger of every major decision you make (discoveries studied, buildings raised, eras entered), worded like city council meeting minutes.
Achievement cards now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b).
Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets text size and reduce-motion back to their defaults in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26).
Fixed the mobile Advance Season button clipping off the right edge of the screen on narrow phones.

New optional City Views panel: a dense numbers dashboard, a top-down civic map of your buildings (a distinct shape per building type), and a Sankey-style resource flow diagram showing how last season's work became food, materials, tools and knowledge.

New: a settlement archive (file your city's stats and a picture of its 3D view in a gallery kept on this device, with delete and clear) and a downloadable shareable card image, both inside the Civilization Summary.

New optional Consulting mode: take over a struggling pre-built city (the Smokestack City or the Sprawling Suburbs) and hold a Steady score for three seasons within thirty. Only offered before you play a season.

Second civic-backlog wave: an isometric camera preset and a pinnable time-of-day light, branch filter chips and exact effects plus unlock estimates on research nodes, a stakeholder-style summary with a Bronze/Silver/Gold efficiency rank, a keyboard shortcuts sheet (press ?), an opt-in community benchmark, a Founder's Log and a time-played readout.

New: optional Civic Challenges (opt-in constraints like taking 20% less from the land, for a knowledge reward), an 'Your city vs. history' chart with a real-world GDP-per-person reference line and its source, a livability-vs-population scatter, nine new research nodes, and small readouts (founded year, output per person, calm-season streak, tree completion).
Research panel decluttered: only nodes you can study right now stay in view; Locked and Known discoveries fold into collapsible sections (searching opens them automatically).
New: civilization summary report, three starting scenarios, an opt-in Hard Mode, a snapshot-to-PNG button for the 3D view, and subtle seasonal lighting.
Mobile: the Advance Season button now docks to the bottom of the screen, plus a site-wide body-padding cascade bug fixed so the dock no longer covers page content.
Settings panel: adjustable text size and a Reduce Motion toggle, consolidated into one panel.
Distinct building meshes for Sanitation Works, plus three named camera presets (Overview/Close-up/Aerial).
Research tree gained a search/filter box for its 40+ nodes.
Achievements added: 19 achievements, in-game panel, unlock toast, hub dashboard link, plus a new "Look Back" UI for revisiting completed eras.
Linked into the main hub nav — title card and review widget, same as every other game.
Visual pass: real low-poly Three.js 3D scenes for all seven eras, a WebGL-unavailable 2D fallback, adjustable text size, and a colorblind-safety audit.

Save/security audit: found and fixed six real save-robustness bugs, including an era-restoration crash, adversarial numeric values, a NaN/Infinity gap, a growth-loop page-freeze, and revisit cross-contamination. Earlier (2026-09-13): Digital era added: Urban Planners and Transit Hubs, with a new urban-sprawl mechanic — the flagship SDG 11 era. Earlier: industrial era added: Factory Workers and Sanitation Works, with a pollution mechanic — the first era where growth and livability trade off directly, not just on the score. Earlier: medieval era added: Guildmasters and Public Works, with the research tree's first resilience-side sustainability bonus. Earlier: Classical era added: Administrators and Canals, with a resilience-side sustainability adjustment; foundations (from 2026-09-02): Foundation shipped: the Tribal-era city simulation, sustainability/livability scoring, the continuous research tree, the save system, and the info-panel shell; then story and era-transition framework: ongoing logs, era-transition beats, and the first full Tribal to Agrarian transition. Earlier: Space Age era added: habitat capacity becomes a new fourth livability provision. All seven eras are now complete.
